Translation-only layout fixture

Each case is a paragraph whose own CSS uses a length that font-size: 0 would otherwise break. Expected notes describe translation only; bilingual must look exactly like before translating.

Centred with auto margins

Good tools stay out of the way. They let readers keep their attention on the text and only appear when they are needed.

margin: 0 auto; max-width: 32em. Expected: the box stays centred on the orange line while the window is resized (was frozen at pixel margins before fix/translation-only-pins).

Percentage padding

Every interruption has a cost. A quiet interface respects the time and focus of the person using it.

padding: 5%. Expected: the tinted padding grows and shrinks with the window (was frozen in pixels before fix/translation-only-pins).

Letter and word spacing in em

Wide spacing makes short headlines feel calm. The translation should keep the same rhythm as the original line.

letter-spacing: .2em; word-spacing: 1em. Expected: the translation keeps the same wide spacing as in bilingual (dropped to normal before fix/translation-only-pins).

Measure in ch

Always-on agents can run for hours. Long lines are hard to read, so articles often limit the measure to a number of characters.

max-width: 40ch. Expected: a normal paragraph, not one character per line (regression check for PR #27).

Fixed width in em

Some layouts give a paragraph a fixed width. The translation should fill the same box rather than collapse to nothing.

width: 24em. Expected: the same box width as in bilingual (pinned in pixels).

Flex items with an em basis

The first card in a row of fixed width cards.

The second card sits next to the first one.

flex: 0 0 14em. Expected: both cards keep their width and stay side by side.

Viewport width (known limitation)

This paragraph is half as wide as the window. In translation only its width is measured once and does not follow later resizing.

max-width: 50vw. Known limitation: frozen at the width it had when translation only was turned on; switching back to bilingual restores it.

Border and radius in em (known limitation)

A framed note with a thick border and rounded corners, both written in em.

border: .5em; border-radius: 1em. Known limitation: the border and corners disappear in translation only (not fixed until a real site needs it).
